description: Team AstroCognition is a research-driven  team under Ajmer Event. Grounded in Environmental Psychology, Organizational Behavior, and Psychophysiology, our mission is to safeguard astronaut health. We are designing a human-centric, autonomous health monitoring system to counter isolation, circadian disruption, and high cognitive workload using NASA Open Data.
summary: COSMO-MIND (Cognitive, Organizational & Somatic Monitoring in Orbit) is an offline-first, autonomous health telemetry and cognitive resilience system for deep-space missions. During Moon and Mars exploration, 4 to 24-minute communication delays make real-time telemedicine impossible, while prolonged isolation and microgravity cause severe physical and cognitive decline.   Built with Python, Streamlit, Pandas, and Plotly, COSMO-MIND integrates a Somatic Engine (Heart Rate, HRV, SpO2, Core Temperature, Sleep) with a Psycho-Cognitive Engine (60-second PVT latency, workload, circadian lighting) into a unified Crew Readiness Index (CRI, 0–100). When clinical or cognitive anomalies occur, it autonomously triggers closed-loop countermeasures like EVA rescheduling and circadian light tuning—ensuring crew safety without cloud dependency.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works: COSMO-MIND (Cognitive, Organizational & Somatic Monitoring in Orbit) is an offline-first, autonomous health telemetry and cognitive resilience software for deep-space missions. Using a Dual-Engine Edge Architecture, its Somatic Engine continuously tracks physical vitals (Heart Rate, HRV, SpO2, Core Temperature, and Sleep Architecture), while its Psycho-Cognitive Engine assesses 60-second Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT) reaction latency, subjective workload, and cabin circadian lighting/noise. A Central Fusion Core synthesizes these signals into a unified Crew Readiness Index (CRI, 0–100) with tri-color alerts (Green 80–100, Yellow 60–79, Red <60). When anomalies occur (such as SpO2 < 93% or >20% PVT latency spikes), the system triggers closed-loop in-habitat countermeasures like EVA rescheduling, circadian light shifts, and guided recovery protocols.

2. Key Benefits:

  • Zero Cloud Dependency: Operates 100% locally on spacecraft edge hardware, overcoming the 4 to 24-minute Earth-to-Mars communication blackout.
  • Prevents Cognitive Overload: Condenses complex multi-sensor biomedical and behavioral data into an intuitive, single-glance CRI score and actionable triage alerts.
  • False-Alarm Reduction: Context-aware noise filtering separates normal exercise exertion from genuine clinical or neuro-cognitive stress.

3. Intended Impact: COSMO-MIND directly supports NASA’s Human Research Program (HRP) goals for Moon (Artemis) and Mars missions by mitigating behavioral health risks, sleep disruption, and cognitive fatigue before they jeopardize critical EVAs or spacecraft operations. Beyond spaceflight, its modular offline architecture can be adapted for extreme terrestrial environments such as polar research stations, submarines, and remote critical-care units.

4. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used:

  • Coding Language: Python 3
  • Software Libraries & Frameworks: Streamlit (interactive mission dashboard UI/UX), Pandas & NumPy (telemetry data processing and CRI fusion modeling), Plotly (real-time interactive time-series visualization), and Git/GitHub (version control and open-source repository hosting).
  • Design & Presentation: Canva (7-slide pitch architecture) and standard local workstation hardware simulating spacecraft edge-computing nodes.

5. How Our Project Is Creative: Unlike conventional space telemetry tools that monitor physical vitals in isolation, COSMO-MIND bridges somatic physiology with organizational and neuro-cognitive psychology into one closed-loop system. Instead of merely displaying passive warning numbers, it acts as an autonomous onboard flight surgeon and behavioral coach—automatically pairing physiological strain with real-time environmental and behavioral interventions (such as dynamic cabin light spectrum tuning and task rescheduling).

6. Key Factors Considered by Our Team:

  • Deep-Space Latency & Bandwidth Constraints: Designing an ultra-lightweight, local edge-processing pipeline that requires zero ground-control connectivity.
  • Astronaut Human Factors & UI Ergonomics: Minimizing visual clutter through high-contrast, color-coded crew status cards tailored for high-stress, microgravity habitats.
  • Clinical & Behavioral Validity: Grounding all biometric thresholds, PVT alertness metrics, and workload scales in official NASA HRP, LSDA, and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) space-health standards.
